title: Quantile-driven Prober & Tail SLA Certification for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers buying Dedicated capacity require documented guarantees at high percentiles (95/99/99.9) across mixed tenant workloads. Existing synthetic throughput runs measure median QPS but do not provide statistical tail certification or per-tenant isolation regressions.

Objective: Build a load-testing harness and benchmarking methodology that certifies Dedicated capacity against tail SLAs with quantified confidence. Deliverables: (1) a reproducible harness that replays tenant-mixed traces and synthesizes adversarial tail behaviors, (2) a standard benchmark suite with dataset/trace provenance, bootstrap-based confidence intervals for quantiles, and (3) an acceptance test checklist and signoff artifact for customers.

Scope: Focus on Dedicated GPU pools and the Redwood serving runtime. Include autoscaler interactions (scale-up/down events), KV/cache warmup windows, and fallbacks to model-variant routing. Do not include private-onprem packaging changes or new billing models in this ticket.

Non-goals: Building a new chaos-injection platform (we will reuse existing instance termination tools), exhaustive customer-specific scenarios (we will provide templates for customers to extend).
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay a 24-hour tenant-mix trace with configurable burst/quiet phases and generate JSON metrics for p50/p95/p99/p99.9 with bootstrap CIs
Benchmarks include at least three representative tenant mixes: steady-state conversational, bursty batch-embedding, and long-context generation
Tail SLA certification report generated automatically: contains quantiles, confidence intervals, sample size, and failure-mode classification
Automated acceptance checklist that a solutions engineer can run for a customer signoff; checklist produced as a markdown artifact in the repo
Integration test that triggers autoscaler events and verifies no P99.9 regression above allowed threshold during scale operations
notes: Architecture: Controller (go) coordinates Scenario runners (k6 + custom Go prober), tenant-mixer (trace player), and metric aggregator (Prometheus -> analysis job). Results stored as GH artifact + Confluence summary.

Harness components:
- Trace player: plays per-tenant request sequences with timing and optional KV cache priming.
- Mixer: merges traces according to specified tenant weight distributions.
- Adversary module: injects pathological sequences (very long contexts / repeated cache misses) to surface tail behavior.
- Autoscaler driver: simulates scaling events and configurable cooldowns.
- Analysis job: computes quantiles with bootstrap resampling and outputs CIs and root-cause tags.

Metric definitions: token-latency (end-to-end), request-latency (inference call), queueing-delay, model-switch latency (time to fallback), percent CPU/GPU utilization per node, KV cache hit ratio per-tenant.

Statistical method: Use bootstrap with 2000 resamples to produce 95% CIs for each quantile. For p99.9 where samples are sparse, run multiple independent 1-hour shards and combine via conservative aggregation (max of shard upper CIs) to avoid false passes.

Provenance: baseline trace set derived from anonymized customer production traces (consent obtained), open synthetic mixes we maintain, and a seed corpus of extreme tail patterns collected from incidents backlog (links in artifacts).

Customer acceptance artifact: single-page PDF that includes a verdict (Pass / Marginal / Fail), observed quantiles + CIs, workload config used, and recommended mitigations (batching, quantization profile, autoscaler tuning).

Runbook outline: preflight (ensure clean cluster, no background experiments), warmup (KV cache priming, model hot cache), steady-state run (3 hours), tail-probe run (30 minutes of adversarial sequences), teardown and artifact collection.
implementation_plan: Week 1: scaffold harness repository, basic trace player, and simple mixer; create initial benchmark configs for 3 mixes
Week 2: add adversary module, autoscaler driver integration, and Prometheus exporters for per-tenant metrics
Week 3: implement analysis job with bootstrap resampling and generate CI reports; begin internal runs
Week 4: integrate customer acceptance checklist, generate first PDF signoff artifact, and validate against internal Dedicated fleet
Post rollout: handoff to Solutions Engineering with runbook and templates for customer-specific trace ingestion
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: p99.9 requires very large sample sizes - mitigation: shard runs and conservative aggregation + clear messaging in certificate
Risk: replayed traces may not capture real tenant resource contention - mitigation: include tenant-affinity mixing and node-level isolation checks
Risk: autoscaler noise confuses signal - mitigation: instrument and correlate scale-event boundaries, treat warmup windows specially in analysis
Risk: long runs consume Dedicated capacity - mitigation: schedule tests to use a staging pool and coordinate with capacity ops
